subsystems.name: Power supply
subsystems.role: converts mains electricity into a high-current, low-voltage DC arc.

subsystems.name: Torch head
subsystems.role: constrains the arc and gas into a precise cutting jet.

subsystems.name: Gas delivery
subsystems.role: supplies the plasma gas and cools the torch.

subsystems.name: Cooling
subsystems.role: removes heat from the torch and power supply.
parts: liquid cooling for higher duty cycles

subsystems.name: Control and safety
subsystems.role: sets current, manages gas flow and prevents electric shock.
parts: current control dial or digital interface

subsystems.name: Work lead
subsystems.role: completes the electrical circuit through the metal being cut.

buildSteps.title: Design the power stage
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose an inverter topology so a small, light unit can deliver 20–50 A at around 100 V DC to the arc.

buildSteps.title: Wind the transformer and inductors
buildSteps.detail: Copper windings are wound on ferrite or iron cores to step voltage down and smooth the current.

buildSteps.title: Make the torch consumables
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes are machined from copper and fitted with a hafnium insert; nozzles are turned from copper or copper-tungsten to a precise bore.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the torch head
buildSteps.detail: Electrode, swirl ring, nozzle and shield cup are stacked with O-rings so gas swirls around the arc and exits as a tight jet.

buildSteps.title: Integrate gas and cooling paths
buildSteps.detail: Internal hoses, valves and heat sinks are fitted so air or coolant reaches the torch and returns without leaks.

buildSteps.title: Wire the control electronics
buildSteps.detail: The trigger, current control, high-frequency start circuit and safety interlocks are connected to the power board.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Each unit is run on scrap steel, its current and gas pressure checked, and the arc stability verified before shipping.

prerequisites.why: compact inverters are needed to make a handheld unit light enough to carry.
air is the usual plasma gas and also cools the torch in low-cost units.
hafnium survives the arc and emits electrons reliably, giving long consumable life.
the bore diameter and concentricity determine cut quality and kerf width.

pathway.milestone: handheld inverter plasma cutters running on mains power cut steel up to about 12–25 mm thick in workshops.
pathway.unlocks: affordable, portable cutting that replaces angle grinders for many tasks.

pathway.milestone: battery-powered or higher-efficiency units with longer consumable life.
pathway.unlocks: cutting in remote locations without a generator.

pathway.milestone: integrated digital controls that automatically set current and gas flow for the material thickness.
pathway.unlocks: easier, more repeatable cuts for less experienced users.

pathway.milestone: robotic or CNC-guided personal plasma tables become common in small workshops.
pathway.unlocks: factory-grade precision at a hobbyist scale.
